name: The Timeline for Your Garage Wall Framing Project
description: The Timeline for Your Garage Wall Framing Project

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Getting your garage walls framed involves a few key phases, and knowing what to expect can really help keep things on track. Let's break it down! First up, Phase 1: Foundation and Preparation. Before any wood goes up, you need to verify your foundation is square and level. This is also when pressure-treated sill plates are anchored to your concrete slab. You'll want to make sure the concrete has cured for at least 7 days, which is pretty standard. Phase 2 is all about the Layout and Assembly. This is where the top and bottom plates are laid out together, and stud locations are marked, typically every 16 inches on center, including all your door and window openings. Then, the studs are cut, fastened to the plates, and any necessary blocking or bracing is added. It’s pretty common to assemble these wall sections right there on the floor. Phase 3 is when you actually see it all come together: Tilting and Fastening. The assembled wall sections are tilted into place, plumbed, and securely fastened to the slab and any adjoining walls. They also get tied into the existing structure and roof framing. Finally, Phase 4: Sheathing and Inspection Prep. Once the walls are up, sheathing is installed, and everything is prepped for the crucial framing inspection. This entire framing process, for a new detached garage, usually takes about 2-5 days after the concrete has cured. Keeping this timeline in mind, and working with experienced pros like HH Remodeling LLC in the Denver metro area, helps ensure your project moves smoothly and meets all local requirements.
